title: Ghonchu, your robotics tutor
what: The course in one notebook: build the base in ten minutes, connect it in thirty, tune it in fifteen. Ghonchu looks at your chassis through your phone's camera.

title: Chassis and vision
what: Wire the motor driver to the pins in the table, then let Ghonchu look at the chassis.

title: Network and telemetry
what: Register your robot on the free backbone and set the safety heartbeat that stops the motors when messages stop arriving.

title: Ghonchu's eye, live
what: Ghonchu watches through the phone camera and speaks when something needs attention. This version checks the light; your own checks go into process_ghonchu_frame.

title: Ghonchu's eye with a vision model
what: The same eye with an open-weight vision-language model (Qwen2.5-VL 7B in 4-bit) on a Colab T4 GPU. Choose Runtime, then Change runtime type, then T4 GPU.

title: Clinical vision assistant
what: For clinicians and medical educators: the assistant looks at instruments, vials, labels and layouts and says one sentence about what it sees. For teaching and practice only.

title: Epigraphy field assistant
what: For historians and archaeologists: point the camera at an inscription, a coin or a sherd, and the assistant names the likely script family and what it can read. Raking light helps.

title: Field linguistics assistant
what: For field linguists: text, symbols and articulation described in one sentence, with IPA where it applies.

title: Psychology observation assistant
what: For psychologists: an objective description of a room or a task set-up. It does not diagnose, and nobody is observed without informed consent.

title: BCI and neuro-vision assistant
what: For BCI and neuroscience work: electrode placement, caps and signal plots, checked for plain faults such as line noise or a loose electrode. The course's robots can be driven by a NeuroSky headset.

title: One tutor for any domain
what: Type the domain you are working in, and the same assistant adapts its prompt to it: robot wiring, surgical trays, Brahmi inscriptions or EEG caps.

title: Systems architecture in SysML
what: Describe a system and get PlantUML for a SysML block definition diagram, compiled and shown in the notebook. The example is a CubeSat.

title: An app from a sentence
what: Describe a web app; the model writes a single-page app, zips it, and the notebook shows how to publish it from a phone.

title: A full stack from a sentence
what: A web front end, a Flask back end and a setup script for a free-tier cloud machine, zipped together.

title: Notebooks as a volunteer grid
what: Nginx in front of a small Flask agent, with a shared sheet as the directory, turns many notebooks into a Beowulf-style or BOINC-style grid.

title: Filling thousands of function stubs
what: For the operating-systems course: every atomic C function is specified by its interface; a loop fills each stub through an API and zips the tree. The first loop discussed is kept below as well.

title: Backbone and mission control
what: The environment cell for the Hindawi toolchain, the free signalling backbone on Sheets and Pages, and one tracker for every embodiment, from a toy robot to a CubeSat.

title: Coding agents and Colab limits
what: Coding agents you can run inside Colab, and the session limits to plan around.
